shots.purpose: Put the audience inside Fuzzby's ride before it knows whose ride it is — establish the scene's grammar as travel, and the flowers themselves as the promise of trouble — he is travelling too fast and too erratically at exactly their height. Carries the work song and the whole chained cause from the over-deep dip to the leaf's FWIP, unbroken, so it reads as one cause and not a list of accidents.
shots.performanceAssignment: He flies the field as a display rather than a commute — chest driving ahead of his own wings, antennae carried proud-erect like rank, mouth working the work song at full throttle, and every zig-zag climbing higher than the flowers need before dropping lower than they need, so he is porpoising up and down inside his own zig-zag with the blossom heads brushing past him the whole way. He aims his head, not his line, at the blossom and drives it in past its centre; the anthers dump their loose gold onto his braced hind legs, and the new weight hanging off his back end swings his exit line sideways so he leaves the bloom flank-first and travelling wrong. His flank meets the broad leaf, the leaf's stalk takes him and bows low, and the bow's rebound throws him back out across the field with the loose gold shearing off him. He arrests himself inside his own falling cloud and rebuilds the on-parade stance from the chest outward — shoulders back, head lifting last, wings still beating fast beneath a body that has decided to be dignified — while one antenna stays folded over and does not come up with its partner. The impact stretches into one slow pocket at the leaf — antenna whipping slow, gold hanging in the air, wings still beating fast through it — then snaps back to full speed for the recovery stance. Nothing freezes; the tempo runs slow and comes back.
shots.camera: The camera opens LOCKED on the pair, front-on, and holds there — no drift, no bank, no push — long enough for the audience to read both bees together and the size gap between them, which is the whole set-up for the payoff. It only moves once he leaves, and then it is Fuzzby's overexcited wingman — pushing continuously closer as the zig-zag climbs into its overshoot, never cutting, banking with him, deliberately half a beat late, horizon rolling as he rolls, and near-field leaves passing close enough to swipe the lens. It genuinely loses him at the dip behind a near-field leaf and rediscovers him already sideways and in trouble — the loss is the point, so his speed reads as something the frame cannot contain. Through the FWIP the camera must be thrown by the leaf's spring rather than choose the move: every inch of travel here has a visible physical cause in frame. Zenny must stay findable and unremarked near his shoulder through the recovery — close enough that she is still readably the smaller of the two — without the camera going to look for her.
shots.openingPose: Both bees hovering at flower-top height in the open field, seen from the FRONT at the same distance from the lens — Fuzzby left of centre and clearly the larger, Zenny to his right and smaller, the size gap plainly readable because they share a depth. Low sun flaring in behind them, open sky above the flower tops, lavender spikes, white daisies and clover heads crowding the frame below them. Wings working hard on both, hovering — he is already loading to go, she is already at her work — and the frame stays with the pair long enough to read them together before he goes — and he goes UP AND AWAY FROM CAMERA into the open sky above the flower tops — climbing, not crossing. He never travels through frame-right where Zenny holds her place, and never crowds off the left edge; the open air above him is where the climb lives. The camera goes with him from that moment, so screen position afterwards is the camera's business, not his. Zenny holds her place on the right throughout.
shots.cutInMotivation: This is the one junction the treatment protects on meaning alone: the dip, the sideways drag and the leaf's spring are ONE cause, and a cut anywhere inside them turns a single continuous physics chain into two unrelated events — the audience would read bad luck instead of overcommitment, and the whole reversal loses its author.

shots.tempoDesign: Fast and accelerating from the first frame: the zig-zag climb runs on quick, uneven up-down beats with no two the same length, tightening as he closes on the blossom. The dip is the one deliberate loading action — a hair longer than the beats around it. From the anthers' dump to the leaf's bow the chain runs continuous with no gaps at the joins: the sideways drag is a fast slide, the leaf's bow is heavy and slow-in as it takes his weight, and its rebound is a hard snap out. The impact runs in a stretched slow pocket of roughly a beat — everything moving, nothing held — then returns to full speed for the recovery, which builds over about a second and a half, the chest first, the head last. The drooped antenna NEVER LIFTS — its partner comes up with the stance and this one simply does not; what arrives a beat AFTER the stance has finished is its own last small sag, so the tell lands on its own timing. Wings beat fast and continuous through every phase, including the slow pocket.

shots.purpose: Button the ricochet with the cover-up, in a frame where the world is still visibly contradicting the claim — and let the boast land at nobody, so the beat hands over a need for a witness.
shots.performanceAssignment: He is holding a pose he has decided is a posture: chest pumped forward and shoulders pinned back, the whole upper body carried in place by effort rather than at rest, with tiny hover corrections drifting him a fraction up and down and his wings beating fast and continuous beneath the dignity. Everything he does is the work of maintaining the claim — jaw set, head high, eyes fixed out front as he delivers the reclaim without any part of the pose loosening. Once, his eyes drop to the folded antenna and come straight back out front, and the head lifts a degree higher to compensate; he flexes the antenna upward from its base, it rises halfway, then folds over again and he refuses to look at it a second time. As the last of the gold sifts past his shoulder his eyes travel off down the corridor to where the other bee is working, and the chest stays pumped while they go.
shots.camera: The camera stops travelling and stays with him at close range because it has just been thrown here — it is out of breath, not composed. What must stay true is that the world keeps contradicting him inside his own frame: the falling gold and the leaf's dying oscillation stay in shot with him for the whole reclaim, so the boast is never allowed a clean background to be true in.

shots.purpose: The boast IS the launch — and the flower has the last word, closing on him. The only impact with no ride before it, and the only one he cannot cover up, because the cover-up is stuck inside a bloom.
shots.performanceAssignment: The claim and the launch are one movement in him: the chest pumps forward on the answer and the pump itself is what drives him, so he is already travelling as the words go out, antennae proud-erect, hind legs trailing, the line rising and dipping under him without ever levelling. What is left outside keeps insisting: his rear half wags side to side against the closed petals as he shoves forward at something he cannot reach, and both wings beat fast and continuous outside the fold, working against a flower that has already won. The wagging gets smaller but does not stop, and the petals do not open.

output.frameLogic:
THE DIRECTOR, PLAIN WORDS FIRST.

(1) WHAT IS THIS FRAME FOR? In the first half-second a four-year-old should feel the floor drop — we are already moving, already behind someone who is going too fast, and stems are coming at us. Not "here is a bee", but "we are IN it". And over the top of the frame, the parent clocks the leaf ceiling pressing down on him and knows, without being told, that this ends badly. The frame is a promise of trouble made by crowding, not by anything anyone does.

(2) WHAT MUST THIS FRAME AFFORD? Twelve seconds of chained physics land on this stage, so the stage has to have the room and the objects already in it:
 · A LANE UP AND AWAY. He is mid-zig-zag, climbing. The performance's first move is up-and-forward into the next porpoise beat, so the upper-middle depth of the corridor must be genuinely open air — I do not decorate that lane. But the ceiling of leaves closes it a short way above him, so the climb has somewhere to go and something to threaten him.
 · THE OBJECTS THE CHAIN NEEDS, PRESENT AND REACHABLE, NOT INVENTED LATER: the target blossom must already be visible ahead up-corridor (he attacks it at the dip); and the BROAD LEAF that takes him — the one whose stalk bows and snaps — must already be hanging in the mid-corridor, on its own stalk, on the side his weighted exit will drag him toward. If those two are not in the plate now, the render invents them mid-shot and the "one cause" reads as bad luck.
 · A NEAR-FIELD STEM SWINGING BACK ACROSS THE LENS. This is the whole "camera is his wingman, half a beat late" grammar stated in one physical object, and it is also the swipe-close danger the felt intent asks for. It must be caught mid-swing-back, still travelling, so motion can continue out of it.
 · DEPTH TO THE HORIZON OF THE CORRIDOR. Zenny lives at the far end. She is not in this beat and must not be looked at — but the corridor has to actually run that far back or the payoff has nowhere to put her.
 · THE ANCHOR FOR THE CHARACTER NOT DRIVING THE ACTION. Zenny is not a spot in the background; she is welded to her own blossom, settled on its rim, sacks loaded, head down into the cup. Whatever that flower does, she goes with it.
 · Fuzzby placed off-centre and off-edge — low-left-of-centre, pitched away from us — so there is air above, air ahead and air behind him. He must NOT be level or controlled: this is mid-climb, nose up, body rolled with the zig.

THE DP ANSWERS.

(3) SHOT SIZE AND LENS. Wide, from bee-height, 24mm, camera travelling forward and slightly behind and below him — chase position. 24mm because it does the two jobs at once: near-field stems and leaves loom huge and rake past the edges (the swipe, the strobe, the stomach), while the corridor still runs deep enough to hold the far blossom where Zenny sits. Longer glass would give me his face and lose the corridor and the ceiling — and the corridor and the ceiling ARE the promise. Camera slightly below him and rolled with his bank so the leaf ceiling sits heavy across the top of frame.

(4) WHAT IS ACTUALLY RESOLVABLE. At a 24mm wide with him small in the corridor, Fuzzby is a silhouette, a colour and an attitude: round body, nose-up pitch, wings a blur, the rope of gold off his hind end. NOT resolvable, therefore NOT written: a specular ping on his spectacle lenses, his eye direction, his mouth mid-word, individual fur. The brief protects "his spectacles stay visible" — at this size that is honoured as the readable dark round shape of the glasses on his silhouette from three-quarter-behind, nothing finer, and I will not creep the size to get more. Zenny at the far end of the corridor is smaller still: pure small soft shape, posture and colour on her blossom rim, head-down — no features whatsoever, and no light on her that pulls the eye. Anything the performance owns — expression, eyeline, mouth, antenna carriage beat-by-beat — I do not write.
